name: Sensed-presence protocol: Thomas with a 10% right bias, then Burst-X (Saroka & Persinger 2013)
origin: Persinger laboratory, Laurentian University; the two-phase sensed-presence protocol of Saroka & Persinger 2013 (summarised in Saroka's 2015 thesis)
summary: The Persinger lab's two-phase sensed-presence protocol (Saroka & Persinger 2013): 30 min of the 'Thomas' pattern through both temporoparietal regions, 10% stronger on the right, then 30 min of the burst-firing (Burst-X) pattern on both sides equally. The paper reports a rise in coherence between the temporal lobes in people who sensed a presence; its main sample was 31 television visitors with no sham group.
notes: The paper used a helmet with four pairs of solenoids, one pair on at a time for 0.5 s. It gave 30 min of the 849-point Thomas pattern at 3-ms points, 'with a slight 10% increase over the right hemisphere', then about 5 min with the blindfold off for a questionnaire, then 30 min of the 289-point Burst-X at 3-ms points 'once every 3000 ms' (Saroka & Persinger 2013 p.4-5 [398-399]). This program plays the Thomas table with a 3-ms pause between repeats (Persinger 2000 p.3 [661]) and the left side at 0.9 of the right. Phase 2 is an 867-ms burst (289 points of 3 ms), then a 3-s pause, equal on both sides. The phases run back to back: the 5-min break does not fit a 60-min program. The burst is rebuilt as this project's rising sweep with the published point duration and length; the point values were never published as numbers, only as a small graph (Persinger 2000 Fig. 2, p.5 [663]). One left-right pair is on at a time (0.5 s each), and the right side is reversed so that the pair's field points through the head. The four sites per side stand for the lab helmet's four solenoids per side on a 7.5 by 5 cm ellipse; the site names are this project's reading. Field: 1 to 5 uT within the part of the helmet filled by the head (p.4 [398]). This program's setting is the peak field 20 mm in front of each coil. The 31 people of experiment 1 came for television programs, 'were aware of the nature of the experiment' and had no sham group (p.4 [398]). Independent sham-controlled tests of God-Helmet-type fields found no field effect (Granqvist 2005, double-blind; Gendle & McGrath 2012, where the experimenter knew the condition). Granqvist tested these two patterns. If phase 1 is unpleasant, press Skip to go to phase 2; stop at once on fear or distress. Not for people with epilepsy or a seizure history, implanted devices, pregnancy, or anxiety or trauma symptoms; have someone nearby.
setting: Seated in a dark, quiet room, blindfolded (the lab used a chamber with the lights off). In the paper the blindfold came off for about 5 min between the two patterns for a questionnaire. The paper's main sample knew the nature of the experiment and had no sham group; the app's Blind option adds one.
schedule: One 60-min session. For a self-test, compare it with a blinded sham session on another day and write down what you experienced before unblinding; at most weekly.
